issues.display_title: Issue #550: Centralize Timeline Post Response Filtering
issues.main_description_html:
Implementation: Centralize Timeline Post Response Filtering

Summary

Added filterTimelinePosts as a package-local helper in PostResponse.go. The helper replaces the repeated response-filtering loop in Most Popular, Recent, and Just For You without changing their queries, flow, allowed fields, or response values.

Changes

PostResponse.go

Added:

func filterTimelinePosts(posts []Models.V1DetailPost, fields []string) []map[string]interface{}

The helper performs the original nested-loop behavior:

  1. Iterate through posts in their existing order.
  2. Create one response map per post.
  3. Iterate through the already validated include fields.
  4. Copy each requested value from Models.V1DetailPost.
  5. Add all three description fields when description is selected.
  6. Return the filtered posts in their original order.

Updated handlers

  • MostPopularPost.go
  • TimeLinePostRecent.go
  • TimeLinePostJustForYou.go

Their repeated mapping blocks now use:

validFields := Functions.GetValidIncludes(include, endpointAllowedFields)
res["posts"] = filterTimelinePosts(postsTimeline, validFields)

The include == "" branch remains unchanged and still assigns postsTimeline directly.

PostResponse_test.go

Added focused coverage that verifies:

  • Selected fields retain their values and types.
  • description still expands into the full, short, and long description keys.
  • visibility, post_count, bookmark, and folder retain their existing values.
  • An empty post result remains a nil slice.

Endpoint-Specific Compatibility

The original switches were behaviorally equivalent but not character-for-character identical:

  • Most Popular and Just For You included a visibility mapping.
  • Recent did not include visibility in its whitelist or switch.
  • Some switch cases appeared in a different source order.

The helper contains the union of the shared mappings, while each caller still controls which fields can reach it through its unchanged whitelist. Therefore, Recent still cannot return visibility, while the other two endpoints can.

Case order does not change the output because each post is represented by a map. Every key still receives the same model property as before.

Response Compatibility

  • Unsupported include fields are still removed by Functions.GetValidIncludes before filtering.
  • A requested description still emits three keys with the same string values.
  • Pointer-backed folder values are passed through unchanged.
  • post_count retains its existing map value and numeric types.
  • Post ordering is unchanged.
  • An empty filtered result remains nil and keeps its previous JSON representation.
  • Without include, the full model response remains untouched.
  • Response messages, envelope keys, encryption input, ls, and viewer e4 behavior are unchanged.

Flow Compatibility

The helper runs only where the old inline filtering loop ran. The following behavior remains outside and before it:

  • Authentication and blocked-content preparation.
  • Pagination.
  • Include validation for query selection.
  • Database query construction and execution.
  • Timeline enrichment, including counts, descriptions, and bookmark state.
  • Existing error responses.

No query, Redis lookup, Elasticsearch call, or response encryption step was moved or changed.

Test-Driven Verification

Tests were added before production code. The first focused run failed because filterTimelinePosts was undefined:

undefined: filterTimelinePosts

After adding the minimum helper, the focused tests passed. The three callers were then changed to use the tested helper.

Scope Audit

  • 1 existing package-local response helper file updated.
  • 1 existing focused test file updated.
  • 3 related timeline handlers updated.
  • Approximately 180 repeated mapping lines removed from the handlers.
  • No new package, dependency, reflection, or global abstraction added.
  • TimeLineListPostProfile was not changed because its model and mapping differ.
  • No Slim, Worker, Support, or unrelated endpoint changed.
  • The existing API collection environment edit was not modified.

Verification

gofmt -w src/Action/V1/Posts/PostResponse.go src/Action/V1/Posts/PostResponse_test.go src/Action/V1/Posts/MostPopularPost.go src/Action/V1/Posts/TimeLinePostRecent.go src/Action/V1/Posts/TimeLinePostJustForYou.go
go test -count=1 -run '^TestFilterTimelinePosts' ./src/Action/V1/Posts
go test -count=1 ./src/Action/V1/Posts
go test -count=1 ./...
go vet ./...
git diff --check

Results:

  • All changed Go files are formatted.
  • Focused response-filtering tests pass.
  • Complete Posts package tests pass.
  • The complete Go test suite passes with no failing package.
  • go vet ./... succeeds.
  • git diff --check succeeds.

Problem

Three related timeline endpoints repeated the same nested loop and field-mapping switch when processing the include query parameter:

  • MostPopularPost.go
  • TimeLinePostRecent.go
  • TimeLinePostJustForYou.go

Each implementation iterated over Models.V1DetailPost, iterated over the validated fields, and copied the same model properties into a filtered response map. Maintaining the mapping in three locations could cause response fields or types to drift.

Scope

  • Add one package-local timeline response filtering helper in the Posts package.
  • Move only the matching Models.V1DetailPost field-to-map mapping into the helper.
  • Update the three related timeline endpoints to use the helper.
  • Keep each endpoint's existing include-field whitelist local.
  • Preserve the unfiltered response path when include is empty.
  • Add focused tests for selected-field mapping and empty-result behavior.

Behavior Boundary

The refactor must preserve:

  • Existing Functions.GetValidIncludes calls and endpoint-specific whitelists.
  • visibility support in Most Popular and Just For You.
  • The absence of visibility support in Recent.
  • Every field name, Go value, pointer, and response type.
  • Expansion of description into description, short_description, and long_description.
  • Ignoring unsupported include fields.
  • A nil filtered slice when no posts are returned.
  • The complete postsTimeline response when include is empty.
  • Existing post order.
  • Existing queries, filters, sorting, pagination, enrichment, errors, messages, and encryption.
  • Existing mobile-facing encrypted and unencrypted response structures.

Out of Scope

  • Combining endpoint-specific include-field whitelists.
  • Updating TimeLineListPostProfile, because it uses a different model and field set.
  • Updating Detail Post, Search, Slim, Worker, Support, or unrelated responses.
  • Changing response fields, JSON names, nullability, or values.
  • Changing database or Elasticsearch behavior.
  • Introducing reflection, generics, or a global response abstraction.

Acceptance Criteria

  • One package-local helper owns the matching timeline field mapping.
  • All three scoped endpoints use the helper.
  • The duplicated nested loops and mapping switches are removed from those endpoints.
  • Each endpoint retains its original include whitelist.
  • Empty and populated filtered results preserve their previous shapes.
  • Queries and response contracts remain unchanged.
  • All changed Go files are formatted.
  • go test -count=1 ./... passes.
  • go vet ./... passes.
  • git diff --check passes.

Delivery

Implemented in the working tree on 2026-09-09. No commit was created.

issues.display_title: Issue #551: Centralize Published Folder Request Setup
issues.main_description_html:
Implementation: Centralize Published Folder Request Setup

Summary

Added preparePublishedFolderRequest as a package-local helper and replaced the duplicated request setup in three Published Folder Bookmark endpoints. The helper returns validation state and request data without writing HTTP responses or changing endpoint-specific behavior.

Changes

PublishedFolderRequest.go

Added:

  • publishedFolderRequest
  • preparePublishedFolderRequest

The result contains:

  • lastLogin for the existing encrypted response metadata.
  • blockPosts for post visibility filtering.
  • notInEncrypt for deactivated and blocked-user filtering.
  • missingSlug so handlers retain their existing HTTP 400 response.
  • unauthorized so handlers retain their existing HTTP 401 response.

Updated handlers

  • PublishedFolderBookmark.go
  • PublishedFolderBookmarkDetail.go
  • PublishedFolderBookmarkContributors.go

Each handler now uses:

request := preparePublishedFolderRequest(c, slug, role, encrypt)
if request.missingSlug {
	return Functions.ErrorResponse(c, 400, fiber.ErrBadRequest.Message, "Bad Request Required Slug")
}
if request.unauthorized {
	return Functions.ErrorResponse(c, 401, fiber.ErrUnauthorized.Message, "Unauthorized")
}
lastLogin := request.lastLogin
blockPost := request.blockPosts
notInEncrypt := request.notInEncrypt

Unused context, time, Redis, user-function, and configuration imports were removed where no longer required.

PublishedFolderRequest_test.go

Added focused tests proving:

  • Missing slug takes precedence over invalid role.
  • Invalid role is rejected before Fiber, Redis, or user-data dependencies are accessed.

Shared Flow

preparePublishedFolderRequest performs the original matching operations in the same order:

  1. Create the default timestamp using the original format.
  2. Report a missing slug.
  3. Reject roles other than user and viewer.
  4. Load deactivated users.
  5. For a user, retrieve data through UserFunctions.UserDatas.
  6. Report unauthorized state when user data is invalid.
  7. Replace the timestamp with the stored last_login value.
  8. Load blocked users.
  9. Load blocked posts.
  10. Append blocked users after deactivated users.

Viewer requests stop after loading deactivated users and retain empty blocked-post data, matching the previous behavior.

Handler Compatibility

  • PublishedFolderBookmark still performs the folder query, folder response shaping, POTD lookup, post count, and total-view aggregation locally.
  • PublishedFolderBookmarkDetail still calculates pagination and loads folder posts after request setup.
  • PublishedFolderBookmarkContributors still parses and clamps its contributor limit after request setup.
  • All handlers still own their exact HTTP errors and encrypted response envelopes.

Query and Response Compatibility

  • publishedFolderPostsBaseQuery is unchanged.
  • Redis key names and GetEncodedStringList behavior are unchanged.
  • Deactivated and blocked-user exclusion order is unchanged.
  • Blocked-post filtering is unchanged.
  • SQL tables, selects, joins, filters, counts, grouping, ordering, limits, offsets, and scans are unchanged.
  • Error codes, messages, and response inputs are unchanged.
  • Response keys, values, types, nullability, encryption input, ls, and viewer e4 behavior are unchanged.

Test-Driven Verification

Tests were added before production code. The first focused run failed because the helper did not exist:

undefined: preparePublishedFolderRequest

After adding the minimum helper, the focused tests passed. The three callers were then changed to use the tested request setup.

Scope Audit

  • 1 package-local request helper file added.
  • 1 focused test file added.
  • 3 related Published Folder handlers updated.
  • No endpoint-specific query or response construction moved.
  • No global utility, reflection, interface, or new dependency added.
  • ListPublishedFolderBookmarkProfile was not changed because its flow differs.
  • No Slim, Worker, Support, or unrelated endpoint changed.
  • The existing API collection environment edit was not modified.

Verification

gofmt -w src/Action/V1/Bookmarks/PublishedFolderRequest.go src/Action/V1/Bookmarks/PublishedFolderRequest_test.go src/Action/V1/Bookmarks/PublishedFolderBookmark.go src/Action/V1/Bookmarks/PublishedFolderBookmarkDetail.go src/Action/V1/Bookmarks/PublishedFolderBookmarkContributors.go
go test -count=1 -run '^TestPreparePublishedFolderRequest' ./src/Action/V1/Bookmarks
go test -count=1 ./src/Action/V1/Bookmarks
go test -count=1 ./...
go vet ./...
git diff --check

Results:

  • All changed Go files are formatted.
  • Focused Published Folder request tests pass.
  • Complete Bookmarks package tests pass.
  • The complete Go test suite passes with no failing package.
  • go vet ./... succeeds.
  • git diff --check succeeds.

Problem

Three related Published Folder Bookmark endpoints repeated the same request preparation flow:

  • PublishedFolderBookmark.go
  • PublishedFolderBookmarkDetail.go
  • PublishedFolderBookmarkContributors.go

Each endpoint validated the folder slug and role, loaded deactivated users, resolved authenticated user data and last_login, loaded blocked users and posts, and built the same user exclusion list. Maintaining this flow in three places could cause authorization and visibility filtering to drift.

Scope

  • Add one package-local request preparation helper in the Bookmarks package.
  • Centralize the matching slug and role validation state.
  • Centralize the timestamp, authenticated user, blocked-user, blocked-post, and deactivated-user setup.
  • Update the three related Published Folder endpoints to consume the prepared request.
  • Keep HTTP response writing in each handler.
  • Keep endpoint-specific queries, pagination, limits, response construction, and encryption in their existing handlers.
  • Add focused tests for validation order and dependency isolation.

Behavior Boundary

The refactor must preserve:

  • Required non-empty slug validation before role validation.
  • Accepted roles: user and viewer only.
  • Existing HTTP 400 and HTTP 401 responses, messages, and order.
  • Default timestamp format 2006-01-02T15:04:05.000000.
  • Retrieval of authenticated user data through UserFunctions.UserDatas for user requests only.
  • Existing unauthorized handling when user data is invalid.
  • Deactivated-user Redis key <prefix>_deactive_users_ec.
  • Blocked-user Redis key <prefix>_blocked_users_ec_<encrypt>.
  • Blocked-post Redis key <prefix>_blocked_post_ec_<encrypt>.
  • Deactivated users before blocked users in notInEncrypt.
  • Viewer behavior without authenticated user, blocked-user, or blocked-post lookups.
  • Existing SQL queries, filters, ordering, pagination, limits, and error responses.
  • Existing encrypted and unencrypted response structures, fields, types, and values.

Out of Scope

  • Updating ListPublishedFolderBookmarkProfile, because it has different roles, target-user validation, and blocking behavior.
  • Updating general bookmark-list endpoints.
  • Moving the helper to Utils, because its validation and returned data are specific to the Published Folder handlers.
  • Replacing existing Redis decoding or fallback behavior.
  • Changing folder, post, contributor, or mobile-facing response contracts.
  • Refactoring Slim, Worker, Support, or unrelated endpoints.

Acceptance Criteria

  • One package-local helper owns the matching Published Folder request setup.
  • All three scoped handlers use the helper.
  • The duplicated setup is removed from those handlers.
  • Missing slug is reported before invalid role and before external dependencies are accessed.
  • Invalid role is reported before Redis or user-data dependencies are accessed.
  • Redis keys, exclusion order, and user-only lookups remain unchanged.
  • Endpoint-specific queries and responses remain unchanged.
  • All changed Go files are formatted.
  • go test -count=1 ./... passes.
  • go vet ./... passes.
  • git diff --check passes.

Delivery

Implemented in the working tree on 2026-09-09. No commit was created.

Implementation: Centralize Profile Following Flow

Summary

Moved the duplicated Profile Following and Search Profile Following behavior into one canonical flow in the Users package. The Search package now delegates to that flow, while a boolean mode enables only the existing search-specific parameter parsing and SQL predicate.

Changes

Users/ProfileFollowing.go

The existing entry point now calls the shared flow without search behavior:

func ProfileFollowing(c *fiber.Ctx) error {
	return profileFollowing(c, false)
}

Added the search entry point:

func SearchProfileFollowing(c *fiber.Ctx) error {
	return profileFollowing(c, true)
}

Added profileFollowing, which contains the matching request validation, user lookup, visibility checks, following query, followed-state lookup, response shaping, and encryption previously duplicated by both endpoints.

The flow decodes usernameFullname only when search mode is enabled.

Added:

func profileFollowingQuery(db *gorm.DB, userID, searchTerm string, searchEnabled bool) *gorm.DB

The helper builds the original shared following query. It adds the existing username and fullname ILIKE condition only when searchEnabled is true.

Search/SearchProfileFollowing.go

Replaced the duplicated implementation with a thin wrapper:

func SearchProfileFollowing(c *fiber.Ctx) error {
	return UsersAction.SearchProfileFollowing(c)
}

Users/ProfileFollowing_test.go

Added focused query coverage proving:

  • Standard Profile Following does not contain an ILIKE predicate.
  • Search Profile Following contains both username and fullname ILIKE predicates.
  • Search mode still adds those predicates when the search term is empty.

Flow Compatibility

The canonical flow retains the original operation order:

  1. Read request metadata and decode the target username.
  2. Decode the search term only for the Search endpoint.
  3. Resolve pagination.
  4. Validate the role.
  5. Load authenticated user data for non-viewer requests.
  6. Look up the target user.
  7. Enforce the my-user ownership rule.
  8. Reject deactivated target users.
  9. Validate the viewer token role.
  10. Check whether the authenticated user blocked the target user.
  11. Query following users with the endpoint-specific search condition.
  12. Apply the deactivated-user exclusion, ordering, limit, and offset.
  13. Resolve followed state in one batch for non-viewer requests.
  14. Build the existing response items and optional hide field.
  15. Return the existing encrypted or unencrypted response.

Viewer requests still skip followed-state lookup. Reading the empty followed-state map produces the same boolean false value previously written explicitly by the Search handler.

Query Compatibility

  • The standard endpoint retains no search predicate.
  • The Search endpoint retains users.username ILIKE ? OR users.fullname ILIKE ? in the same query position.
  • Search mode remains explicit even for an empty term. This preserves the original ILIKE '%%' behavior and avoids including rows where both searchable columns are NULL.
  • Tables, selected columns, joins, banned-user filtering, deactivated-user filtering, ordering, pagination, and scan types are unchanged.

Response Compatibility

  • Response messages, status codes, envelope keys, values, and types are unchanged.
  • following, followed, and conditional hide fields retain their existing shapes.
  • Viewer followed remains boolean false.
  • Encryption input, ls, and viewer e4 behavior are unchanged.
  • No mobile-facing response contract changed.

Test-Driven Verification

The focused test first failed because profileFollowingQuery did not exist:

undefined: profileFollowingQuery

During compatibility review, the test was expanded to require the empty-search predicate. That test failed against the initial helper signature before searchEnabled was added. The final helper preserves the distinction between a standard request and a Search request with an empty term.

Scope Audit

  • 1 canonical Users flow added inside the existing handler file.
  • 1 focused Users test file added.
  • 1 duplicated Search handler reduced to a thin wrapper.
  • No global utility, interface, reflection, or dependency added.
  • Profile Follower was not changed because its behavior differs.
  • No Slim, Worker, Support, or unrelated endpoint changed.
  • The existing API collection environment edit was not modified.

Verification

gofmt -l src/Action/V1/Users/ProfileFollowing.go src/Action/V1/Users/ProfileFollowing_test.go src/Action/V1/Search/SearchProfileFollowing.go
go test -count=1 -run '^TestProfileFollowingQuery' ./src/Action/V1/Users
go test -count=1 ./src/Action/V1/Users ./src/Action/V1/Search
go test -count=1 ./...
go vet ./...
git diff --check

Results:

  • All changed Go files are formatted.
  • Focused Profile Following query tests pass.
  • Users and Search package tests pass.
  • The complete Go test suite passes with no failing package.
  • go vet ./... succeeds.
  • git diff --check succeeds.

Problem

The Profile Following and Search Profile Following endpoints duplicated the same request and response flow across different packages:

  • Users/ProfileFollowing.go
  • Search/SearchProfileFollowing.go

Both endpoints decoded the target username, validated roles, resolved authenticated user data, checked deactivated and blocked users, queried following users, resolved followed state in one batch, shaped the response, and handled encryption. The Search endpoint only added a username and fullname search predicate. Maintaining both implementations separately could cause authorization, visibility, followed-state, or response behavior to drift.

Scope

  • Make the Users package the canonical owner of the Profile Following flow.
  • Add one package-local flow that supports the standard and search variants.
  • Keep the existing Users.ProfileFollowing entry point for the standard endpoint.
  • Add a Users.SearchProfileFollowing entry point for the search variant.
  • Replace the duplicated Search implementation with a thin delegation to the canonical flow.
  • Isolate the query difference in one package-local query helper.
  • Add a focused test for standard and search query behavior.

Behavior Boundary

The refactor must preserve:

  • Existing username and search-term URL decoding and errors.
  • Existing accepted roles and validation order.
  • Existing authenticated-user and viewer behavior.
  • Existing target-user lookup and my-user ownership check.
  • Existing deactivated-user and blocked-user checks, Redis keys, and errors.
  • Existing SQL table, selected columns, join, filters, ordering, pagination, and scan model.
  • No search predicate for the standard Profile Following endpoint.
  • Both users.username ILIKE and users.fullname ILIKE predicates for Search Profile Following, including an empty search term.
  • Existing batch followed-state lookup for non-viewer requests.
  • A boolean false followed state for viewer requests.
  • Existing hide field behavior for blocked-user data.
  • Existing messages, status codes, response fields, values, types, encryption input, ls, and viewer e4 behavior.

Out of Scope

  • Updating Profile Follower, because its blocked-user processing order and error handling differ.
  • Changing database queries, response contracts, or mobile-facing behavior.
  • Changing role, blocking, deactivation, pagination, or encryption rules.
  • Moving this endpoint-specific flow into a global utility.
  • Refactoring Slim, Worker, Support, or unrelated endpoints.

Acceptance Criteria

  • One canonical flow owns the matching Profile Following behavior.
  • Both endpoint entry points use the canonical flow.
  • Search package contains only a thin delegation for this endpoint.
  • Standard Profile Following does not add a search predicate.
  • Search Profile Following retains both ILIKE predicates, including for an empty term.
  • Response structures, values, types, and endpoint flow remain unchanged.
  • All changed Go files are formatted.
  • go test -count=1 ./... passes.
  • go vet ./... passes.
  • git diff --check passes.

Delivery

Implemented in the working tree on 2026-09-09. No commit was created.

Implementation: Centralize Timeline Request Setup

Summary

Added prepareTimelineRequest as a package-local helper and replaced the duplicated request setup in four related Posts endpoints. The helper returns request data and unauthorized state without writing HTTP responses or moving endpoint-specific behavior.

Changes

TimelineRequest.go

Added:

  • timelineRequest
  • prepareTimelineRequest

The result contains:

  • lastLogin for existing encrypted response metadata.
  • blockPosts for blocked-post query filtering.
  • notInEncrypt for deactivated-user and blocked-user filtering.
  • unauthorized so each handler retains its existing HTTP 401 response.

The helper accepts the handler's existing default lastLogin value. This keeps timestamp creation at the same point in each endpoint flow and replaces it only with stored user data for authenticated requests.

Updated handlers

  • MostPopularPost.go
  • MostPopularPostFeed.go
  • TimeLinePostRecent.go
  • TimeLinePostJustForYou.go

Each handler now uses:

request := prepareTimelineRequest(c, role, encrypt, lastLogin)
if request.unauthorized {
	return Functions.ErrorResponse(c, 401, fiber.ErrUnauthorized.Message, "Unauthorized")
}
lastLogin = request.lastLogin
blockPost := request.blockPosts
notInEncrypt := request.notInEncrypt

Unused context, user-function, and Redis imports were removed where no longer required.

Endpoint-specific work retained

  • MostPopularPost still loads bookmark data and enables bookmark enrichment for user requests.
  • TimeLinePostRecent still loads bookmark data and enables bookmark enrichment for user requests.
  • TimeLinePostJustForYou still loads followings before bookmark data for user requests.

  1. Preserve the handler's default lastLogin.
  2. Reject roles other than user and viewer.
  3. Load deactivated users.
  4. Return immediately for a viewer.
  5. Load authenticated user data for a user.
  6. Return unauthorized state when user data is invalid.
  7. Replace lastLogin with the stored value.
  8. Load blocked posts.

  • Encryption input, ls, and viewer e4 behavior are unchanged.
  • No mobile-facing response contract changed.

The focused test was added before production code. Its first run failed with:

After adding the minimum helper and updating the four handlers, the focused and package tests passed.

issues.display_title: Issue #554: Centralize Place List Query Filters
issues.main_description_html:
Implementation: Centralize Place List Query Filters

Summary

Added placeListQuery to build the shared views_place_list query conditions once. The count, nearest, and global branches now use the helper while retaining their existing projections, aggregation, radius handling, sorting, pagination, and responses.

Changes

GetPlaceList.go

Added:

func placeListQuery(
	db *gorm.DB,
	search string,
	categoryID int64,
	excludedUsers []string,
	nearest bool,
) *gorm.DB

The helper:

  1. Starts from views_place_list.
  2. Applies category_id when the validated ID is positive.
  3. Applies location_group ILIKE for a search value.
  4. Applies location_group IS NOT NULL when search is empty.
  5. Applies stored latitude and longitude validity conditions in nearest mode.
  6. Applies encrypt NOT IN when excluded users exist.

Updated query paths

The count query now starts with:

countQuery := placeListQuery(Config.DB, search, categoryID, notInEncrypt, nearestMode)

The nearest data query uses the same helper with nearest mode enabled before adding its select, grouping, radius HAVING, order, limit, and offset.

The global data query uses the same helper with nearest mode disabled before adding its select, grouping, order, limit, and offset.

GetPlaceList_test.go

Added a local PostgreSQL dry-run database helper and focused tests proving:

  • Search, category, latitude, longitude, and user-exclusion predicates are present when enabled.
  • Empty search retains location_group IS NOT NULL.
  • Optional category, coordinate, and exclusion predicates are absent when disabled.

Flow Compatibility

The handler still performs operations in the same high-level order:

  1. Read and validate query parameters.
  2. Validate category existence when supplied.
  3. Validate the request role.
  4. Load deactivated and blocked users.
  5. Execute the total-place count query.
  6. Execute either nearest or global data query when results exist.
  7. Shape and return the existing response.

No database query was added or removed.

Query Compatibility

  • Count still uses COUNT(DISTINCT location_group).
  • Nearest and global select expressions are unchanged.
  • Nearest and global grouping remains location_group, location_group_slug.
  • Search, category, coordinate validity, and exclusion predicates retain the same values and semantics.
  • Radius greater than zero remains a row-level WHERE condition for count.
  • Radius greater than zero remains an aggregated HAVING condition for nearest data.
  • Sort selection and tie-break ordering are unchanged.
  • Limit and offset behavior are unchanged.

The helper uses one consistent ordering for SQL AND predicates. PostgreSQL evaluates these predicates as the same conjunction, so returned rows and totals remain unchanged.

Response Compatibility

  • statusCode, data, messages, data_places, total, valid, and version remain unchanged.
  • Full and include-filtered place models retain their existing values and types.
  • Contributor shaping and overflow calculation are unchanged.
  • Encrypted and unencrypted response envelopes are unchanged.
  • No mobile-facing response contract changed.

Test-Driven Verification

The query tests were added before production code. Their first run failed with:

undefined: placeListQuery

After adding the minimum helper and routing all three query paths through it, the focused tests passed.

Scope Audit

  • 1 existing Places handler file updated.
  • 1 existing Places test file updated.
  • 3 query paths now share the same base filter helper.
  • No response code, model, route, global utility, configuration, or dependency changed.
  • No Search Location, Place Detail, Slim, Worker, Support, or unrelated endpoint changed.
  • The existing API collection environment edit was not modified.

Verification

gofmt -w src/Action/V1/Places/GetPlaceList.go src/Action/V1/Places/GetPlaceList_test.go
go test -count=1 -run '^TestPlaceListQuery' ./src/Action/V1/Places
go test -count=1 ./src/Action/V1/Places
go test -count=1 ./...
go vet ./...
git diff --check

Results:

  • Changed Go files are formatted.
  • Focused Place List query tests pass.
  • Complete Places package tests pass.
  • Complete Go test suite passes with no failing package.
  • go vet ./... succeeds.
  • git diff --check succeeds.

Problem

GetPlaceList.go repeated the same views_place_list filters across three query paths:

  • Total-place count query.
  • Nearest place data query.
  • Global place data query.

Each path independently applied search, category, deactivated-user, and blocked-user conditions. The count and nearest paths also repeated coordinate validity conditions. Maintaining these conditions separately could make total disagree with data_places when one query path changed without the others.

Scope

  • Add one package-local placeListQuery helper in GetPlaceList.go.
  • Centralize the shared table and filter construction.
  • Use the helper for count, nearest, and global query paths.
  • Keep radius handling in the count and nearest callers.
  • Keep select lists, grouping, sorting, pagination, scans, and responses in their existing paths.
  • Add focused dry-run query tests for required and optional filters.

Behavior Boundary

The refactor must preserve:

  • The views_place_list source table.
  • Category filtering only when a valid positive category_id is present.
  • location_group ILIKE filtering for a non-empty normalized search value.
  • location_group IS NOT NULL when search is empty.
  • Latitude and longitude non-null and non-empty filters only in nearest mode.
  • Deactivated-user and blocked-user exclusion through encrypt NOT IN when the exclusion list is non-empty.
  • Radius filtering with WHERE in the count query.
  • Radius filtering with aggregated HAVING in the nearest data query.
  • No radius or coordinate filtering in global mode.
  • Existing category validation, role validation, Redis lookups, and authenticated-user handling.
  • Existing select expressions, grouping, sorting, pagination, limits, offsets, and scan models.
  • Existing response fields, values, types, errors, messages, and encryption.

The helper may normalize the textual order of SQL AND predicates. All predicates and values remain equivalent, so query results and API behavior remain unchanged.

Out of Scope

  • Changing the Haversine expression or distance calculation.
  • Combining radius WHERE and HAVING behavior.
  • Refactoring response shaping or contributor processing.
  • Updating Search Location, Place Detail, Slim, Worker, Support, or unrelated endpoints.
  • Moving this query-specific helper to global Utils.
  • Adding a dependency or changing the API contract.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Count, nearest, and global queries all use placeListQuery.
  • Search, category, coordinate validity, and excluded-user behavior remain equivalent.
  • Empty search still excludes null location_group values.
  • Nearest mode still validates stored coordinates.
  • Radius behavior remains outside the helper and unchanged for count and data queries.
  • total and data_places use the same base filters.
  • All changed Go files are formatted.
  • go test -count=1 ./... passes.
  • go vet ./... passes.
  • git diff --check passes.

Delivery

Implemented in the working tree on 2026-09-09. No commit was created.

Implementation: Centralize Content Visibility Setup

Summary

Added ResolveContentVisibility to the global Functions utility and routed seven matching handlers through it. The former Posts-only timeline helper was removed because the shared flow now serves Posts, Broadcast, and Search.

Changes

Functions.go

Added ContentVisibility with:

  • LastLogin
  • BlockedPosts
  • ExcludedUsers
  • Unauthorized

Added:

func ResolveContentVisibility(c *fiber.Ctx, role, encrypt, lastLogin string) ContentVisibility

The utility accepts the existing handler-created lastLogin. Viewer requests retain that value, while authenticated user requests replace it with stored user data.

Updated handlers

  • MostPopularPost.go
  • MostPopularPostFeed.go
  • TimeLinePostRecent.go
  • TimeLinePostJustForYou.go
  • DetailBroadcastPost.go
  • ListBroadcastBookmark.go
  • SearchLocationPost.go

Each handler now consumes the same result:

visibility := Functions.ResolveContentVisibility(c, role, encrypt, lastLogin)
if visibility.Unauthorized {
	return Functions.ErrorResponse(c, 401, fiber.ErrUnauthorized.Message, "Unauthorized")
}
lastLogin = visibility.LastLogin
blockPost := visibility.BlockedPosts
notInEncrypt := visibility.ExcludedUsers

SearchLocationPost retains its original early role validation before parsing search and pagination parameters. The utility is called at the original Redis setup position, preserving dependency timing.

Removed Posts-only helper

Removed:

  • src/Action/V1/Posts/TimelineRequest.go
  • src/Action/V1/Posts/TimelineRequest_test.go

Their responsibility and focused validation test moved to the global Functions package.

Functions_test.go

Added TestResolveContentVisibilityRejectsInvalidRoleBeforeDependencies, proving that an invalid role:

  • Returns unauthorized state.
  • Preserves the caller-provided lastLogin.
  • Returns before Redis or Fiber-dependent user-data access.
  • Leaves blocked-post and excluded-user data unset.

Shared Flow

ResolveContentVisibility performs the existing matching operations in this order:

  1. Preserve the handler's default lastLogin.
  2. Reject roles other than user and viewer.
  3. Load deactivated users.
  4. Return immediately for a viewer.
  5. Load authenticated user data for a user.
  6. Return unauthorized state when user data is invalid.
  7. Replace lastLogin with the stored value.
  8. Load blocked posts.
  9. Load blocked users.
  10. Append blocked users after deactivated users.

Compatibility

  • No database query was added, removed, or changed.
  • Selected columns, visibility filters, blocked-content filters, user exclusions, ordering, pagination, and scan models remain unchanged.
  • Bookmark and following calls remain endpoint-specific and retain their existing order.
  • Response structures, values, types, nullability, messages, errors, and status codes remain unchanged.
  • Encryption input, ls, and viewer e4 behavior remain unchanged.
  • No mobile-facing response contract changed.

Scope Audit

Handlers with different behavior were intentionally excluded. Examples include bookmark lookup interleaving in SearchPost, blocked-user-first lookup in Hashtag handlers, target-block validation in Likes handlers, and processing branches in DetailPost.

No Slim, Worker, Support, dependency, configuration, route, model, or schema was changed. The existing API collection environment edit was not modified.

Test-Driven Verification

The focused global utility test was added before production code. Its first run failed with:

undefined: ResolveContentVisibility

After adding the utility and updating the seven handlers, focused package tests and the complete suite passed.

Verification

gofmt -w src/Utils/Functions/Functions.go src/Utils/Functions/Functions_test.go src/Action/V1/Broadcast/DetailBroadcastPost.go src/Action/V1/Broadcast/ListBroadcastBookmark.go src/Action/V1/Posts/MostPopularPost.go src/Action/V1/Posts/MostPopularPostFeed.go src/Action/V1/Posts/TimeLinePostJustForYou.go src/Action/V1/Posts/TimeLinePostRecent.go src/Action/V1/Search/SearchLocationPost.go
go test -count=1 ./src/Utils/Functions ./src/Action/V1/Posts ./src/Action/V1/Broadcast ./src/Action/V1/Search
go test -count=1 ./...
go vet ./...
git diff --check

Results:

  • All changed Go files are formatted.
  • Focused package tests pass.
  • Complete Go test suite passes with no failing package.
  • go vet ./... succeeds.
  • git diff --check succeeds.

Problem

Seven related content endpoints used the same request setup for authorization and visibility filtering:

  • MostPopularPost.go
  • MostPopularPostFeed.go
  • TimeLinePostRecent.go
  • TimeLinePostJustForYou.go
  • DetailBroadcastPost.go
  • ListBroadcastBookmark.go
  • SearchLocationPost.go

The flow validates the user or viewer role, loads deactivated users, resolves authenticated user data and last_login, loads blocked posts and users, and builds the same excluded-user list. The four Posts handlers already shared a package-local helper, but the same flow remained duplicated in Broadcast and Search.

Scope

  • Promote the matching request setup into a reusable utility in src/Utils/Functions/Functions.go.
  • Update all seven handlers to use the global utility.
  • Remove the superseded Posts-only timeline helper and migrate its focused test.
  • Keep endpoint-specific queries, bookmarks, followings, response shaping, and encryption in their existing handlers.
  • Leave similar handlers with different validation or lookup order unchanged.

Behavior Boundary

The refactor must preserve:

  • Accepted roles: user and viewer only.
  • Existing HTTP 401 response structure and message for invalid roles or invalid user data.
  • Each handler's existing default lastLogin creation point.
  • Deactivated-user Redis key <prefix>_deactive_users_ec.
  • Blocked-post Redis key <prefix>_blocked_post_ec_<encrypt>.
  • Blocked-user Redis key <prefix>_blocked_users_ec_<encrypt>.
  • Redis lookup order: deactivated users, user data, blocked posts, then blocked users.
  • Deactivated users before blocked users in the exclusion list.
  • Viewer behavior without user-data, blocked-post, or blocked-user lookups.
  • Existing SQL queries, filters, projections, ordering, pagination, and scan models.
  • Existing response keys, values, types, status codes, messages, errors, and encryption.

Out of Scope

  • Moving bookmark, following, target validation, or endpoint-specific state into the utility.
  • Changing Redis decoding or fallback behavior.
  • Changing database queries or mobile-facing API contracts.

issues.main_description_html:
Implementation: Centralize Notification Query and Mapping

Summary

Added package-local helpers for the notification base query and common row mapping. ListNotifications and ListNotificationMonth now reuse those helpers while retaining their different filters, post data, response envelopes, and encryption behavior.

Changes

NotificationPost.go

Added:

func notificationListQuery(db *gorm.DB, userID string, excludedUsers []string) *gorm.DB

The helper builds the shared query with:

  1. notifications n as the source.
  2. Left joins to sender users and related posts.
  3. Recipient-user filtering.
  4. User and post banned-state filtering.
  5. Optional sender exclusion through u.encrypt NOT IN.

Also added:

func buildNotificationData(notification Models.NotificationQuery) (map[string]interface{}, error)

The helper parses created_notif_dt and maps these common fields:

  • id
  • read
  • notification_type
  • body
  • created_at
  • created_notif_dt
  • post_id
  • userBySenderId

ListNotifications.go

The handler now uses notificationListQuery for its base query and buildNotificationData for each row.

The handler still owns:

  • type and nt normalization.
  • Notification-type SQL filtering.
  • Deactivated and blocked sender exclusions.
  • Conditional notification visibility rules.
  • Conditional total count behavior.
  • Full and slim post fields.
  • Existing response and encryption variants.

The helper receives a nil exclusion list in this handler so the existing notification-type predicate remains before sender exclusion in the query construction sequence.

ListNotificationMonth.go

The handler uses the same base query and row mapper. Its existing exclusion list is passed directly to notificationListQuery.

The handler still owns:

  • Unconditional notification visibility rules.
  • Total notification count.
  • Thumbnail and notification-type-specific slug handling.
  • pw field removal.
  • Versioned encryption through query parameter v.

Query Compatibility

  • Selected columns remain endpoint-specific and unchanged.
  • Both handlers retain the same table, joins, predicates, parameters, ordering, limits, offsets, and scan model.
  • ListNotifications retains notification-type filtering before its sender-exclusion predicate.
  • ListNotificationMonth retains sender exclusion before visibility rules.
  • Count and data retrieval remain on the same query paths as before.
  • No database query was added or removed.

Response Compatibility

  • Common notification fields retain their original values and Go types.
  • created_at still uses CreatedAtUTC().
  • created_notif_dt still uses the 2006-01 layout.
  • Invalid month data still returns the same HTTP 500 error message.
  • ListNotifications still adds visibility and its full or slim post representation.
  • ListNotificationMonth still adds thumbnail and slug fields according to notification type.
  • Existing nil post_id, pw, sl, nt, type, and v behavior remains unchanged.
  • Response envelopes, messages, status codes, and encryption inputs remain unchanged.
  • No mobile-facing response contract changed.

Tests

NotificationPost_test.go now verifies:

  • Shared notification table, joins, recipient filter, banned filters, and sender exclusion.
  • Common mapped field values and types.
  • UTC timestamp formatting.
  • Month formatting.
  • Sender data mapping.

Test-Driven Verification

The focused tests were added before production code. Their first run failed with:

undefined: notificationListQuery
undefined: buildNotificationData

After adding the helpers and updating both handlers, focused package tests and the complete test suite passed.

Scope Audit

  • 2 notification handlers updated.
  • 1 existing package helper file updated.
  • 1 existing test file updated.
  • No global utility, interface, dependency, configuration, route, model, or schema added.
  • Notification-post batch retrieval remains unchanged.
  • Slim, Worker, Support, and unrelated endpoints were not changed.
  • The existing API collection environment edit was not modified.

Verification

gofmt -w src/Action/V1/Notifications/ListNotificationMonth.go src/Action/V1/Notifications/ListNotifications.go src/Action/V1/Notifications/NotificationPost.go src/Action/V1/Notifications/NotificationPost_test.go
go test -count=1 ./src/Action/V1/Notifications
go test -count=1 ./...
go vet ./...
git diff --check

Results:

  • Changed Go files are formatted.
  • Focused Notifications package tests pass.
  • Complete Go test suite passes with no failing package.
  • go vet ./... succeeds.
  • git diff --check succeeds.

Problem

ListNotifications.go and ListNotificationMonth.go repeated the same notification-list foundation:

  • Querying notifications n.
  • Joining sender users and related posts.
  • Filtering by recipient user and banned states.
  • Optionally excluding blocked or deactivated senders.
  • Parsing created_notif_dt.
  • Building the common notification and sender fields.

The endpoints have different filters and response variants, but maintaining their identical base query and row mapping separately could cause shared behavior to drift.

Scope

  • Add one package-local base query helper in the Notifications package.
  • Add one package-local common response-mapping helper.
  • Update ListNotifications and ListNotificationMonth to use both helpers.
  • Keep endpoint-specific filters, post fields, response shaping, and encryption in their existing handlers.
  • Add focused tests for shared query filters and mapped field values.

Behavior Boundary

The refactor must preserve:

  • The notifications n source table.
  • Existing LEFT JOIN operations to users and posts.
  • Recipient-user, user-banned, and post-banned predicates.
  • Existing deactivated-user and blocked-user exclusion behavior.
  • Notification-type and visibility-rule behavior in ListNotifications.
  • Unconditional visibility rules in ListNotificationMonth.
  • Existing count timing, ordering, pagination, and scan models.
  • Existing created_at UTC formatting and created_notif_dt parsing.
  • Existing sender field values and types.
  • Existing post, thumbnail, slim, pw, nt, type, and v behavior.
  • Existing response keys, values, types, errors, status codes, and encryption.

Out of Scope

  • Combining both handlers into one endpoint.
  • Standardizing their different query parameters or response contracts.
  • Changing notification visibility rules.
  • Changing notification-post batch retrieval.
  • Moving package-specific helpers to global Utils.
  • Refactoring Slim, Worker, Support, or unrelated APIs.

Acceptance Criteria

  • notificationListQuery owns the shared base query.
  • buildNotificationData owns common notification row mapping.
  • Both notification-list handlers use the helpers.
  • Each handler retains its endpoint-specific filters and response fields.
  • Invalid created_notif_dt retains the existing HTTP 500 response.
  • Query results and API responses remain unchanged.
  • Focused helper tests pass.
  • All changed Go files are formatted.
  • go test -count=1 ./... passes.
  • go vet ./... passes.
  • git diff --check passes.
